# Review — cid-tiradas-18-18 (lines 295–403)

## Pass 1 — units.json

**Continuity (after edits):** PASS. 38 units; concatenated `t` = the packet's 109 lines exactly, in print order
(298b included; 395 before 394; 398 absent, printed by Pidal in tirada 19); every `l` has as many lines as its
`t`; all units 1–4 lines; one tirada, the first unit opens it. `t` untouched (checked by script against the draft
as received).
Assonance re-derived from all 109 line-endings: á throughout (Bivar, valdrá, sonrisar … juntar, posar), with á-e
counting as the same assonance (sale, heredades, sabe, madre, laudare, cárçel, Calvarie, partes, alguandre, sangre,
padres, padre, carne, Fáñez) and Pidal's paragogic [e] in vv. 325–339. The claim in u1 is correct; the comparison
with ó/ó-e in tiradas 14 and 17 checked against the published notes.
Every cross-reference (49 citations, vv. 2–395) was checked against the published parts and the packets; all point
to the line they describe. One was apt for its construction but placed so as to mislead (u10, v. 169).
Bracket claims (dont a ojo los ovo, plaz[d]o, Se[e]d, me[m]brados, Qu[o]mo, [ensellar], the paragogic [e]s, f[o],
[te], [C]aspar, [de], para[d]iso, nu[n]qua, vi[d]o, [oviste], resuçit[ar], [cr]ebanteste, cre[d]o, vi[d]iestes,
buen[a], pie[n]ssen, [han]) say that Pidal restored the letters; one gave Pidal a motive (u12), now removed.
Names: the published parts have Alvar Fáñez in `t` and Álvar Fáñez in `i`, and no Minaya yet; the draft's
"Minaya Álvar Fáñez" (u30) and "Álvar Fáñez" (u33) conform. Formula renderings conform ("You were born of your
mother in a good hour", u30; "the spiritual Father", u3, u27).
Readings flagged uncertain in the notes, and kept so: tornós a sonrisar 'began to smile' or 'smiled again' (u2);
the construction of v. 303 (u3); the subject of creçió (u4); ca 'but, whereas' (u19); a tan grand sabor (u30);
tornólas a catar 'turned to look' or 'looked again' (u27); quieren cavalgar 'want' or 'are about to' (u25); the
location of the places on the road (u37, now also the Roman road).

### Considered and refused
- "Minaya Álvar Fáñez" in u30 i. Kept: the published `i` fields write Álvar Fáñez (pilot v. 14), and Minaya is in the text; dropping it would lose a word, and "Albar" would break with the published spelling.
- Title/part "Ximena" against the packet header's "Jimena". Refused: as in the 15-17 review; the text and the published parts say Ximena.
- u17 i "my lord Saint Sebastian" adds "my". Refused: the English title of reverence for señor san; l keeps "lord saint".
- u14 i "Father who art in heaven" is the stock Lord's Prayer wording. Kept: the note says the line echoes the Lord's Prayer; the echo is the point.
- u14 n: prayers of this kind in the French chansons de geste. Kept: accurate and minimal.
- u30 n: Minaya "usually explained as mi + anaya". Kept: presented as the usual explanation, not as fact.
- u36 n: Sant Estevan = San Esteban de Gormaz on the Duero. Kept: the standard identification, and the Duero crossing follows in v. 401.
- u5 n: "six days gone and three to come make nine". Kept: simple arithmetic on the text.
- u24 i "grant that we be joined again" for nos faz juntar ('make us join'). Kept: a prayer's imperative to God; l is literal.
- u11 n: los mediados gallos "between midnight and dawn". Kept: what 'middle cockcrow' means; no hour invented.
- u20 n: the Longinus legend (blind, healed by the blood). Kept: it is the story the next lines tell, and the note says the Gospel does not name him.

## Pass 2 — gloss.json

Keys = the 255 novel-forms.json keys exactly, plus `__broaden__`. Every token of the 109 lines (brackets stripped,
lowercased, apostrophe split) is covered by gloss.json or known-forms.json, with no extra keys. Every entry checked
against its line(s) and the units' notes. All 30 draft broadens began with the old entry whole + " · "; 6 broadens
added for known forms used in a new sense; all 36 re-checked by script. Continuity re-run after Pass 2: PASS (109/109).

### Considered and refused
- nasquiestes lemma "nacer", reçebir "recebir", against the notes' nasçer, reçebir. Refused: spelling of the lemma, not a contradiction (as in the earlier reviews).
- alcobiella "= Alcubilla". Kept: the usual identification (Alcubilla del Marqués, near San Esteban de Gormaz); the units' note already says not every place can be located with certainty.
- fin "(fem. in Old Spanish)". Kept: true of Old Spanish and harmless, though the gender cannot be seen in this line.
- priessa "a una priessa 'all in one bustle'" against the note's 'with a haste so great'. Refused: a gloss of the phrase a una priessa alone; not a contradiction.
- sobre broaden "'above, hard by Navas de Palos'" against the note's 'at'. Refused: compatible.
- arabia "the eastern land from which the Magi came". Kept: the poem's own claim; the note gives Matthew 2.
- Known entry maría "Santa María, the cathedral of Burgos". Not broadened: "Mary" already covers v. 333; the santa broaden names the Virgin.
